fixes.explanation: Verse 1 says it plainly: Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah "…were leaders of the people." Out of twenty-five men at that gate, these are the two the text names. What the LORD says about these men comes next, and it's serious.

I get the guess, friend, since they're standing right at a gate. But standing at a gate doesn't make you a gatekeeper. I stand next to my ovens all day and nobody hands me an oven keeper's badge. The text says these two were leaders of the people.
No instruments and no songs show up anywhere in this scene. Verse 1 calls Jaazaniah and Pelatiah leaders of the people. And what the LORD says about them next is not a tune.

The LORD says, "…these are the men who plot evil and give wicked counsel in this city." Plotting is planning ahead, and here the plan is evil. God tells Ezekiel, the prophet in this vision, exactly what these men are doing. Nothing is hidden from Him.
Counsel just means advice. The LORD calls their advice wicked. That's the word in verse 2: they "…give wicked counsel in this city." Advice from the wrong people gets expensive fast.
That one flips the whole sentence around. Hating evil would be the opposite of what the LORD describes. Verse 2 says they "plot evil," so they're planning it, not pushing it away.

I can see how you got there, but the LORD does the opposite. In verse 4 He says, "Therefore prophesy against them; prophesy, O son of man!" He says "prophesy" twice. These men don't get left alone. They get a message from God.

That's what God says in verse 5: "…I know the thoughts that arise in your minds." He's speaking to the house of Israel, and He knows what goes on in their minds. I can walk into my kitchen and forget why I came in. God never loses track of a single thought.

That's it. The men said, "The city is the cooking pot, and we are the meat." Then verse 7 says, "The slain you have laid within this city are the meat, and the city is the pot; but I will remove you from it." God uses the same picture, puts the slain in it, and says the men will be removed.
Right. In verse 7 God says, "but I will remove you from it." Verse 11 adds, "The city will not be a pot for you, nor will you be the meat within it." They're headed out.
Verse 8 says, "You fear the sword, so I will bring the sword against you, declares the Lord GOD." What they feared is exactly what God says He will bring. This is a heavy part of the passage.
Ezekiel says in verse 13, "Now as I was prophesying, Pelatiah son of Benaiah died." Pelatiah is one of the two leaders named at the gate. This is a heavy moment.
The text doesn't say anything about Pelatiah repenting. Verse 13 says Pelatiah son of Benaiah, one of the two leaders named at the gate, died while Ezekiel was prophesying. It's a sobering line.

Yes. Ezekiel falls facedown and cries, "Oh, Lord GOD, will You bring the remnant of Israel to a complete end?" I think this is a prayer from a man shaken by what just happened. The next thing in the text is the word of the LORD coming to him.

Calling the exiles leaders isn't in what the people said. In verse 15 the people of Jerusalem say, "They are far away from the LORD; this land has been given to us as a possession." That's what God repeats to Ezekiel.
No crown in this promise, friend. Crowns are fancy, but God has something else in mind. In verse 17 He says, "…I will give back to you the land of Israel." Land is what He gives back.

Glass doesn't show up in this verse, friend. After taking out the heart of stone, God says, "…and give them a heart of flesh…" A glass heart would be see-through and easy to shatter, but that's not the promise. Flesh is the word.

Verse 23 says, "And the glory of the LORD rose up from within the city and stood over the mountain east of the city." The glory had stopped at the east gate of the house of the LORD earlier in the vision (Ezekiel 10:19). Now it rises from within the city and stands over the mountain to the east.

Yes. Verse 25 has Ezekiel saying, "I told the exiles everything the LORD had shown me." He doesn't hold a single piece back. A vision like this, the gate, the pot, the new heart and the glory rising, goes straight to the exiles.
